correctness.rationale: The cyclic-run upper bound covers every source. Even lengths split into pure alternating with exactly two outputs and other words with at most n-2 runs. Odd lengths with n-1 runs have forced 00(10)^{m-1}1 form and two disjoint deletion collisions for m>=4; others have <=n-3 runs. The two-defect family 0^a(10)^t1^b has exactly 2(t+1) distinct run-deletion classes by unique anchored long-run profiles, providing sharp witnesses. Small exceptions are checked directly. A separate finite checker exhausts 4,807 necklace sources through length 15 and witnesses through 300.

The linear one-deletion run maximum n becomes two for a purely alternating necklace; the sharp cyclic outdegree n-2 or n-3 and odd parity obstruction require a new argument. Residual priority uncertainty for unindexed necklace subsequence-order work is explicit.

value.rationale: The all-length exact maximum is the natural outdegree of the binary circular single-deletion observation graph. It quantitatively distinguishes cyclic from linear support, exhibits a nontrivial odd-length obstruction and gives explicit extremal families. This is an unlimited-parameter sharp theorem, not an arbitrary finite slice or recomputation of a known table.
